 Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli odds, prediction, time: Boxing picks for Oct. 31 fight card via top expert
 SportsLine's Josh Nagel reveals his Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli best bets for Saturday at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
 By
 Daniel Kohn 
 Oct 31, 2026
 at
 1:10 pm ET 
 •
 3 min read
 Imagn Images 
 Canelo Alvarez will battle Christian Mbilli for the WBC super middleweight title in a scheduled 12-round bout in the main event on Saturday. The main card is set for 1 p.m. ET from at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia and will be streamed on DAZN pay-per-view. Alvarez (63-3-2) will look to regain his WBC super middleweight title he lost with a unanimous decision defeat to Terence Crawford on Sept. 13, 2025. Mbilli (29-0-1), meanwhile, had won the WBC interim super middleweight title in June 2025 with a first-round knockout of Maciej Sulecki.  Alvarez is a -320 betting favorite (wager $320 to win $100), while Mbilli is priced at +230 (wager $100 to win $230) in the latest Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli odds. The over/under for total rounds finished is 10.5 (-475/+300). The favored method of victory is Canelo via KO/TKO/DQ at +350.  Now, with the Alvarez vs. Mbilli fight card approaching, Nagel has studied Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli from every angle and revealed his top betting picks and best bets.  Head to SportsLine to see them .
 Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli preview 
 Alvarez, 36, has been dominant throughout his long career. He first fought professionally in October 2005 when he knocked out Abraham Gonzalez in the fourth round. He followed that up with three more wins before a split decision draw with Jorge Juarez on June 17, 2006. He then went on to win his next 38 bouts before losing a 12-round major decision to Floyd Mayweather Jr. on Sept. 14, 2013.
 He rebounded and did not lose again until May 7, 2022, in a unanimous decision to Dmitry Bivol for the WBA (super) light heavyweight title. In 68 career fights, Alvarez has posted a 63-3 record, including two draws. He has registered 39 wins by knockout. Six of his last eight wins came by unanimous decision.  Check out SportsLine to see Nagel's picks and analysis. 
 Mbilli, 31, began his professional career with a second-round knockout of Adrian Arenas on Feb. 9, 2017. He has yet to lose a fight, and is 29-0 with one draw. He has registered 24 wins by knockout. Mbilli, who has been highly decorated, won his first title in May 2018, when he knocked out Marcos Jesus Cornejo for the vacant WBA Youth middleweight crown.
 He later won the vacant WBC Youth Intercontinental middleweight title, and then WBC Francophone middleweight crown. In September 2021, he knocked out Ronny Landaeta for the WBC Continental Americas super middleweight championship. He defended that title eight times, before claiming the WBC interim super middleweight title.  You can only see Nagel's picks and analysis at SportsLine .
